description: The one board vocabulary (ADR-048 DEC-8.4). board_profile is the value of /etc/suderra/board in the signed OS image, the provisioning manifest board, the release statement board_profile and the release artifact name (artifact-naming.json); every other vocabulary (Suderra OS build targets, USB payload families, cloud DeviceModel, RAUC compatible, cargo features, Rust target) is mapped onto it here and nowhere else. cloud_provisioning is the cloud's provisioning gate: the manifest service issues a manifest only for a board whose gate is open, and never for a board_profile that matches a pending family's pattern (SG-3).
identity_cross_check_rule: The image declares these values in /etc/suderra/board. At boot the live device-tree compatible (ARM) or DMI vendor/product (x86) must equal one of them; otherwise the agent runs in degraded mode and an alarm result is written (DEC-8.2). The list is never empty: a board without a cross-check value is not a board.
feature_rule: cargo_features is the exact feature set of the build: a release is built with --no-default-features and --features set to this list, and the signed release statement names the same list (release-profile-mismatch). The build must need no feature beyond it: a feature every Suderra OS build requires is implied by the suderra-os feature in the crate's Cargo.toml, as a feature dependency, and is never added by the release pipeline on top of this list. The agent crate currently does not compile without its health feature (EDGE-HIGH-128), so suderra-os must imply health and the release plan's crate_required_features must go; until then the signed statement misstates the build, which sens-api-gateway/release/edge-release.toml records as a tracked defect with an owner and a deadline.
interface_role_rule: Every Ethernet interface of a board has the board's default_interface_role until a signed suderra.site-netpolicy.v1 maps it to another role (DEC-11.6): the default is wan for every board, as every interface has been the WAN/IT side since the single DHCP network unit of P0, and a board-specific fixed port-to-role mapping needs a qualified port-to-NIC fact that no board has yet, so none is declared. The effective role of an interface is the entry of the policy's interfaces[] that matches its MAC or PCI path, otherwise the default; a policy whose effective roles leave the device no wan interface, or that matches one interface twice, is refused (interface-mapping-invalid).

os_runtime.description: The runtime every Suderra OS image provides to the agent binary (ADR-048 DEC-8.5, INFRA-MEDIUM-253): the C library and the shared libraries a release binary may link, for the architectures the images are built for. scripts/edge/edge_release.py reads this table and checks every built binary against it (ELF NEEDED, the program interpreter and the highest GLIBC symbol version), so a dependency that needs anything else fails the release before a device does; the generic channel keeps its own glibc cap and its armv7 runtime in sens-api-gateway/release/edge-release.toml. The values describe the Buildroot 2025.05.3 toolchain of every image (glibc 2.41, BR2_TOOLCHAIN_BUILDROOT_GLIBC on all boards) and the gcc runtime. Suderra-OS tests/image-contracts/os-runtime-contract-test.sh compares this table with the images' build inputs (Buildroot's glibc package version and the toolchain and defconfigs that select it); comparing the libraries of a built rootfs needs the image build and is not done yet, so INFRA-MEDIUM-253 stays open for that part.

cloud_provisioning.reason: Provisioning is open; until SG-1 opens at P2 exit the cloud signs only monitoring-only site configs for it.
How the TPM-less RPi4/CM4 is used in production is an open operator decision (ADR-048 Soru 3, DEC-8.11); the cloud issues no manifest for it until that decision amends this gate.
CI and dev target: only the fake cloud of the QEMU e2e test (Suderra-OS tests/qemu/fake_cloud.py) provisions it, and no DeviceModel maps to it.
No x86 unit is installed in the field before P1 exit (SG-3): the cloud issues no manifest for any board_profile matching board_profile_pattern.

pending_board_families.status: No industrial x86 model is selected or qualified (DEC-8.1, DEC-8.9). Each qualified model becomes its own boards entry x86-ipc-<model> with its own RAUC compatible suderra-os-x86-ipc-<model> and DMI allowlist in a later contract version, so one model's image never installs on another (DEC-8.3). The model-independent x86 image below is the kernel and Secure Boot qualification base and declares no board_profile.

excluded_os_images.reason: Unsupported template with no board, kernel or acceptance path; it runs no agent.
USB self-installer that flashes the rpi4 and revpi4 payload images; it runs no agent.

usb_payload_board_families.description: The board_family and compatible_models vocabulary of the Suderra-OS USB installer payload index (board/suderra/common/post-image.sh, scripts/ci/package-usb-installer-payload.py, suderra.usb-payload-index.v1). It predates boards.json; this is its only mapping onto board_profile.

unmapped_device_models.reason: No Suderra OS image targets the RevPi Compact; such devices stay on the generic-Linux channel (DEC-28).
No Suderra OS image targets the Raspberry Pi 5; generic-Linux channel only (DEC-28).
The SX1302 LoRa concentrator needs the lorawan and sx1302-vendor-hal features, which no Suderra OS profile builds; generic-Linux channel only (DEC-28).
No Suderra OS image targets the Raspberry Pi 5 and no profile builds LoRa; generic-Linux channel only (DEC-28).
Unknown hardware has no signed board identity, so the cloud never issues a Suderra OS manifest for it (DEC-8.2).
